issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor declaration in the template header does not match its implementation: example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) while example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). This mismatch prevents successful compilation of the example program and conflicts with the solution repository which uses the two-argument constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor declaration and definition consistent. Either change example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) to match the .cpp, or implement a matching three-argument constructor in Bitmap24.cpp (and update usages). Prefer aligning the template header to the two-argument signature used in the solution and implementations to avoid compilation failures.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor is declared with a different signature in the template repository header than its implementation and than the solution. In example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp (template) the constructor is declared as Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) (three parameters), but the implementation in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp (template) defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (two parameters). The solution repository uses the two-argument constructor in its header and implementation. This mismatch is an unintended API/identifier inconsistency for the same conceptual entity (the Bitmap24 constructor) and will confuse students and can cause compilation/link errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Recommended: change the template header declaration to match the two-argument constructor used in the implementation and in the solution: declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); (remove the unused 'depth' parameter). Alternatively, update the implementation to provide a matching three-argument constructor if a 'depth' parameter is intentionally required, and ensure both template and solution use the same signature.
